Photograph: Alex Brandon/AP Donald Trump Capital One says it closed Trump Organization’s accounts after anti-money-laundering review Disclosure from 2021 investigation marks first time a bank has formally tied money-laundering concerns to Donald Trump Reuters Sat 1 Aug 2026 20.04 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Capital One Financial hit back on Friday against a lawsuit over its ⁠decision to close the Trump ⁠Organization’s bank accounts ​years ago, stating that it did so after a review by anti-money-laundering experts. The disclosure marks the first time a bank has formally tied money-laundering concerns to Donald Trump ’s family business. Capital One is seeking to dismiss the case by casting doubt on claims of illegally debanking – or denying services on religious or political grounds – the Trump Organization. The Trump Organization and ⁠Capital One did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Capital One has never accused the Trump Organization of money laundering. ​But Friday’s filing argues that “documents and Plaintiffs’ own ‌allegations make clear that Capital One closed ‌Plaintiffs’ accounts for anti-money laundering (‘AML’) reasons. “The closures were the result of months of analysis and a careful review by ‌Capital One’s AML team in accordance with bank policies and regulatory guidance.” Capital One gave notice of its plans to close more than 300 Trump-affiliated bank accounts in March 2021. The Trump Organization and Eric Trump, the president’s son, filed a lawsuit in March 2025 in a Florida federal court, alleging the accounts were closed because of Capital One’s “woke” beliefs and its desire to benefit from the political mood after the 6 January 2021 riot at the US Capitol. Capital One said in Friday’s filing that the Trump Organization’s allegations of political pretext were “misguided” and “based on cherry-picked quotations unsupported by the full context” of documents submitted to the court. “The transaction patterns identified by Capital One are among the types of activity flagged by federal banking guidance,” the filing said. Since the start ⁠of Trump’s second term, his administration has put pressure on some large banks, echoing conservative complaints ​that the institutions are deliberately targeting ​the political right. Trump signed an executive order in ​August 2025 barring discriminatory debanking. In January, Trump filed a suit against JPMorgan Chase on the same ​grounds, underscoring the fraught policy ‌environment Wall Street is ​navigating during the president’s second ​term. In 2019, during his first term, Trump sued Capital One and Deutsche Bank in an attempt to prevent them from sharing financial records with Congress as part of a probe led by Democratic lawmakers. Anti-money-laundering professionals at Deutsche Bank reportedly flagged a set of transactions, but executives ignored them; Deutsche Bank denied the report at the time. The shower gel is perfect for holidays, as I never get bitten when I use it.' bristolpost Bookmark Share What's On By Lauren Codling 04:33, 22 AUG 2026 Updated 10:01, 22 AUG 2026 Bookmark A popular shower gel is fast becoming a summer travel staple after reviewers reported staying completely bite-free on holiday (Image: YakobchukOlena via Getty Images) Liz Earle has long been a trusted name in beauty, celebrated for its botanical skincare range and the iconic Cleanse and Polish Hot Cloth Cleanser. Now, devotees of the British brand can snap up £85 worth of products for significantly less with a special offer, saving £36. The Orange Flower Collection combines five skincare and bodycare staples, all featuring the refreshing fragrance of orange flower. Priced at £49 and available from Liz Earle and John Lewis, the set is billed as an everyday collection designed to revitalise any beauty regime, working out to just £9.80 per item. Leading the lineup is the Orange Flower Cleanse and Polish Hot Cloth Cleanser (valued at £34). This beloved creamy formula works to deeply cleanse while gently exfoliating, leaving the complexion feeling smooth and revitalised - making it an especially appealing choice for devoted Cleanse and Polish enthusiasts. Also included is the Orange Flower Hand Repair (valued at £22), an intensive hand cream that deeply moisturises while nourishing the nails. The lightweight 150ml formula slips easily into a handbag for a touch of everyday indulgence. For the bathroom, there's the Orange Flower Botanical Body Wash (valued at £18), formulated to cleanse and soften the skin. This pairs perfectly with the Orange Flower Botanical Body Cream (valued at £22), which provides nourishing hydration post-bath, the Liverpool Echo reports. Liz Earle Beauty Co Shop here The Orange Flower Collection includes: Orange Flower Cleanse & Polish™ Hot Cloth Cleanser, 200ml Orange Flower Hand Repair™, 50ml Orange Flower Botanical Body Wash, 200ml Orange Flower Botanical Body Cream, 200ml Pure Cotton Cloth £49 Liz Earle Beauty Co Buy Now Completing the collection is a pure cotton cloth, ideal for use with the Cleanse and Polish . A charming blue bag is also provided to keep everything neatly together. In addition to Liz Earle, Lookfantastic offers a wallet-friendly beauty box worth exploring. The You Deserve It Edit costs £35 but boasts a value of £125, featuring brands including Colour Wow, KIKO and Sol De Janeiro. Alternatively, the Boots K+J Beauty Skin Edit ( £35 ) showcases some of the most prominent Korean and Japanese skincare brands, such as Beauty Of Joseon, Curel and Dr Jart. The bundle includes the Orange Flower Botanical Body Wash and the Orange Flower Botanical Body Cream (Image: Liz Earle Beauty Co) Returning to Liz Earle: The Orange Flower Collection has already garnered excellent feedback from customers. One enthusiastic Orange Flower devotee commented: "I love love love shower gel and body cream. "The shower gel is perfect for holidays, as I never get bitten when I use it. I have used Liz Earle for nearly forty years. I'm on holiday and trying out the face sunscreen." Another customer remarked: I've been using Liz Earle for a few years now. It cleanses your face really well, and most of their products are really easy to use. I've never had a reaction to them. The Orange Flower Hand Repair works hard to soften hands and condition nails (Image: Liz Earle Beauty Co) Separately, someone who purchased it as a present confessed: "I love the orange flower from Liz Earle; it's my absolute favourite out of everything. My dry, wrinkled hands are now soft and wrinkle-free." Meanwhile, a devoted user of the Botanical Body Cream remarked: "This is the best body cream I have ever used. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.text: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said if Putin agreed to the energy ceasefire then Ukraine would do the same. Photograph: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters View image in fullscreen Volodymyr Zelenskyy said if Putin agreed to the energy ceasefire then Ukraine would do the same. Photograph: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters Ukraine Trump announces partial ceasefire in Ukraine war as Zelenskyy says deal is ‘news to me’ Ukrainian president earlier rejected US call for Kyiv to stop bombing oil refineries, saying Moscow must first end attacks on energy infrastructure US politics – live updates Luke Harding Sun 11 Oct 2026 11.56 EDT Last modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 12.13 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Donald Trump has announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia, apparently without consulting Volodymyr Zelenskyy , who said the deal to stop long-range attacks was “news to me”. In a social media post, the US president claimed the two sides had reached an agreement. “Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine . Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!” he wrote on Truth Social. He offered no further details. Zelenskyy said he was surprised by the announcement but would agree to it if Vladimir Putin did the same. “If President Trump negotiated it with Putin – please tell us when the ceasefire begins. We are ready and we will accept it,” the Ukrainian president told the Axios website. Earlier, Zelenskyy rebuffed Trump’s demand made on Saturday that Kyiv stop bombing Russian oil refineries. Zelenskyy said Moscow had to first halt its own “brutal” attacks on his country’s energy infrastructure. Any deal to end long-range drone strikes by Ukraine on targets inside Russia would have to be “reciprocal”, he said. It should be backed by “real guarantees” – meaning punitive measures against Moscow from Ukraine’s allies, including the US. View image in fullscreen The aftermath on Sunday of a Russian strike on Kharkiv that hit residential homes. Photograph: Vyacheslav Madiyevskyy/Reuters This is not the first time Trump has announced an energy ceasefire deal. He made the same claim in September, which turned out to be untrue. Ukrainian officials said Russia was still bombing Ukraine on Sunday, with several energy sites damaged. The fast-moving row between Washington and Kyiv began on Friday when Trump announced he was lifting sanctions on Russian diesel exports . He said the move would reduce global and domestic fuel prices before next month’s US midterm elections. A furious Zelenskyy called the decision “weak” and said it would generate “billions” in extra revenue for Putin, enabling him to wage war “even more intensely”. An equally irate Trump said Zelenskyy should “damn well stop” hitting Russian refineries. Ukraine needed a “new leader” , he said on Saturday. Map of Ukraine with Russian advances and territory Responding to Trump, Zelenskyy said it was up to Ukrainians to choose “one or another leader”. He told ABC News he was willing to accept Trump’s demands and to organise elections, but only if Putin agreed to a “total” 60-day ceasefire. The bitter public feud is the most serious between the US and Ukraine since last year, when Trump berated Zelenskyy in the Oval Office . The New York Times has reported that US officials have offered the Kremlin lucrative economic incentives in exchange for a ceasefire. They reportedly include releasing billions in Russian sovereign assets that are frozen. The Trump administration also revisited a plan to sell parts of Russia’s energy company, Lukoil. The multibillion deal would benefit Middle Eastern investors, the paper reported , some with “business ties” to US negotiators. View image in fullscreen Medics help a woman injured in a Russian attack on a residential area in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine on Saturday after overnight strikes. Photograph: Daryna Naumova/EPA On Saturday, Trump berated Zelenskyy and said he had refused to make a deal to end the fighting. In response, Ukraine’s president laid the blame for Europe’s biggest war since 1945 on “Russia and Russia alone”. “It is possible to stop strikes on energy infrastructure as early as today, but Putin does not want to do so,” he said. Ukrainian officials point out that the White House is demanding Kyiv give up its most effective weapon, without demanding any corresponding concessions from Russia. In recent weeks, Kyiv has dealt a major blow to Russia’s economy, striking oil complexes, warehouses and datacentres. Russia’s own bombing campaign has been relentless. On Saturday it killed 23 people in the city of Zaporizhzhia, including four children, and hit a five-storey apartment block in the frontline town of Sloviansk. Zelenskyy said Moscow’s aerial campaign involved thousands of aerial bombs and jet-powered drones. It continued “unabated”, he said. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day after newsletter promotion ‘A life-or-death race’: the volunteers protecting Kyiv’s skies from new jet-powered drones Read more The head of Ukraine’s foreign affairs committee, Oleksandr Merezhko , said Trump’s “bullying” demand for Zelenskyy to quit had strengthened him at home “paradoxically”, after recent damaging corruption scandals. “Putin’s plan is to decapitate Zelenskyy and remove him as a wartime leader. Trump is siding with Putin,” Merezhko said. He added: “I’m afraid that behind this situation is Trump’s worldview. He wants to do business with Putin. For him, Ukraine seems like an obstacle to be removed. Both Trump and Putin wish to pressure us into capitulation.” Referring to the notorious 1939 agreement between Nazi Germany and the USSR, Merezhko said: “We are moving to a new Molotov-Ribbentrop pact and to a world of strongmen and spheres of influence.” Merezhko said Ukraine would continue to destroy enemy oil refineries, against US wishes, because they funded Russia’s war machine and acknowledged that a cutoff of US intelligence sharing with Kyiv – threatened by the Trump administration – would “blind” Ukraine’s air defence systems. “This would be an act of complicity with Putin’s genocide. It would mean more dead civilians and dead children,” he said. Ukrainian negotiators had been meeting in Florida with their American counterparts, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, when Trump announced the US was lifting sanctions on Russian diesel. Blindsided, the Ukrainians went home early. “It felt like a trap,” one stunned Ukrainian official told the Kyiv Independent newspaper . On Saturday, Zelenskyy shored up support in a series of conversations with key European allies including the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, France’s president, Emmanuel Macron, and the Finnish president, Alexander Stubb. Downing Street said Burnham recognised the last 24 hours had been “difficult” for Ukraine and “reiterated his complete solidarity”. Downing Street said the two leaders agreed “to maintain pressure on Russia” and to strengthen the sanctions regime, despite Trump’s efforts to the contrary. “Russia should agree to an immediate energy ceasefire, ending its brutal strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure and its attacks on shipping in the Black Sea,” a statement added. Speaking over the weekend, Zelenskyy said Trump’s decision empowered Putin and gave him “extra money for the war”, running into millions and “perhaps billions”. “It is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should act. And, in my view, it is a weak decision,” he said. https://www.theguardian.com/politics/202.text: Burnham said: ‘Looking back at Brexit … I don’t think it has played out as people said it would at the time.’ Photograph: House of Commons/PA View image in fullscreen Burnham said: ‘Looking back at Brexit … I don’t think it has played out as people said it would at the time.’ Photograph: House of Commons/PA Brexit Brexit deal is not good enough for British public, says Andy Burnham EU exit has damaged economy and failed to bring promised benefits, says PM, but he rules out big pre-election changes UK politics live – latest updates Europe live – latest updates Aletha Adu Political correspondent Mon 26 Oct 2026 05.30 EDT Last modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 06.28 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Brexit has not “played out” like it was promised to the public, has weakened the economy and the current deal is not good enough, Andy Burnham has said, while ruling out any major changes in the current parliament. The prime minister said Britain had ended up with a “harder Brexit than was proposed in the referendum campaign” and it had not helped to control the small boats crisis. Backing the home secretary’s tougher immigration rules , he said Brexit had weakened the UK’s ability to control its borders as it could no longer send people back to Europe. When asked directly on Monday whether he wanted Britain to rejoin the EU, Burnham told Good Morning Britain: “I’ve said I’m going to be honest and say, in my lifetime I would like to see that happen, but I am not going to move ahead of the public. I am not going to dictate in terms of my own opinions here, you have to make sure that the British public are the bosses.” Explaining why he even brought up the possibility of “going all the way” in terms of closer relations with the EU, Burnham said: “Looking back at Brexit … I don’t think it has played out as people said it would at the time. We got a harder Brexit than was proposed in the referendum campaign. “It’s weakened our economy. It’s also weakened our control of immigration, and that might surprise people because that was the big issue, but the small boats crisis has risen since and we have a different form of immigration now.” He added: “I am not going to say at the moment that the deal we’ve got is good enough for Britain. I don’t think it is good enough.” Burnham said he would not “move away from the red lines in Labour’s manifesto”, adding: “I’m not proposing rejoining [the EU] in this parliament. We’re way, way away from that at this particular point in time. What I am saying is we need to take some practical steps to make the arrangement work better.” There are concerns among Labour MPs who represent leave-voting constituencies in the north of the England and the Midlands that reopening the Brexit debate could create opportunities for Reform UK. Asked about the fact that 65% of his constituents in Makerfield voted to leave the EU, the prime minister said: “I said we wouldn’t rerun the referendum and that’s not what I’m doing. The British public, the people of Makerfield, will be the bosses here. They will decide what happens in relation to Brexit … What I can do though is make practical steps to make the arrangements work better.” Emphasising the negative impact Brexit had had on Britain’s control of immigration, the Labour leader said: “I think we’ve got weaker control now. The reason the small boats crisis has arisen is because we can’t return people, and people know we can’t do that in the same way that we used to be able to.” Burnham said he hoped the UK-EU summit on 20 November could yield a deal “which would be good for British food manufacturers, because they’ve been hit hard by Brexit”. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion He said he backed “the principle” of the home secretary’s controversial plan to make foreign workers wait 15 years to get permanent residency. Burnham said Shabana Mahmood was right to pursue the plans based on the principle that “settlement is a right to be earned not just something that is granted automatically”. He also ruled out calling an early general election, despite polling suggesting Labour was still enjoying a “Burnham bounce” . “There is no election coming anytime soon. People may as well put that out of their mind.” On Wednesday’s budget, Burnham said it would offer people and businesses “breathing space”, claiming it would give Britain “a little bit of light at the end of the tunnel”. https://eaworldview.com/2026/10/ukraine-.text: Ukraine War, Day 1,695: White House Ordered Restriction of Starlink to Kyiv Posted by Scott Lucas | Oct 16, 2026 | 0 Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky and Donald Trump at the Mar-a-Lago resort, Palm Beach, Florida, December 28, 2025 (Jonathan Ernst/Reuters) EA-Frontline VideoCast: Allying with Putin, Trump Betrays Ukraine EA on International Media: Selling Out Ukraine — Trump Buys Russia’s Diesel Fuel and Cuts Off Intelligence EA on Australia’s ABC: Ukraine — Russia’s War in the Black Sea Thursday’s Coverage: Zelensky — Trump Has “Betrayed” Us UPDATE 1624 GMT: Pope Leo XIV has appealed to Vladimir Putin for a ceasefire allowing the delivery of food and medical assistance into Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine. Expressing his “grave concern”, the Pope asked for voluntary and safe evacuation of the civilian population of the city in the Kherson region. Oleshky had a pre-invasion population of 24,000. Around 2,000 civilians, including 50 children, remain in the city and its surrounding villages. Residents have sent messages that they are eating weeds in an effort to survive. Ukrainian military authorities have attempted airdrops of emergency food, water, and medical supplies with large drones. It is unclear how much of the aid has been intercepted by the Russian military. UPDATE 1454 GMT: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says that he sees “no willingness on the Russian side to end this war”. Against this backdrop, I believe it is appropriate, logical, and understandable for Ukraine to strike targets within Russia that hinder the war effort of the Russian government and the Russian army – including both communication and energy supply systems…. [This is] the only means Ukraine has to signal to Russia that it is prepared to defend itself. UPDATE 1451 GMT: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky has asked the European Union for another €70 billion ($79 billion) next year to fund Ukraine’s defense against Russia. Zelensky told EU leaders that the war will cost €155 billion ($174 billion) in 2027: “And we need at least €70 billion more from you – for defense, for weapons, and for our resilience. This is a realistic amount.” UPDATE 1431 GMT: In his closed-door address to European Union leaders, Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky implicitly addressed the Trump camp’s apparent betrayal of Ukraine: I am grateful to all of you who are trying to keep Europe and the United States together. There are so many people with good hearts in America who sincerely want evil to lose and Ukraine to stand strong. These are the very hearts that helped Europe defend its freedom and that fought on D-Day, won the Cold War, and won what is best for Europe. Hearts that want to be allies, not to divide or humiliate Europe, and I believe most Americans still feel this way. And at the end of the day, the American people will have their say. Putin will listen to America if America really turns up the heat on him and makes one thing clear: either he chooses peace or he gets no more money for his war. UPDATE 1412 GMT: Asked about Donald Trump’s attacks on him, including that he is supposedly more difficult to deal with than Vladimir Putin, Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky said: I’m only standing up for Ukraine’s interests. And no matter how Russia would like to limit all of our rights, it’s clear that we do have a right to defend ourselves. He explained that Vladimir Putin “does not seek negotiations in any format” but only “playing these games of words”: “He does not want the war to end.” Zelensky asked about the Trump diesel deal with Russia, which could be followed by gas agreements or other attempts to lift sanctions on Russia or its frozen assets, “If I don’t stand up to this, if I don’t defend it, who else will do this diplomatically?” He continues that Russia’s demands are not just about territory but about “our country’s existence”. Putin “wants to destroy us” and “does not respect our sovereignty and territorial integrity”. The President summarized, “We’re now standing and fighting. What’s the alternative? Annihilation.” UPDATE 1144 GMT: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky has spoken about air defense and the White House’s restrictions on Starshield, the military service of Starlink. He said of the critical situation with air defense interceptors, “We are picking them up where we can: one or two here, five there, ten there, arranging all of this and bringing them to Ukraine.” Zelensky said Ukraine’s requests for further help are “the bare minimum” needed. He was confident that European countries have enough interceptors to share and “go through this winter”. He said that Starshield has been restored, but not yet to previous speeds needed for the frontline and air defenses. Starlink was not turned off, but the speed limits were lowered…and we were incapable of shooting down some Shahed drones, and were no longer able to use one of the tools to protect our population. Jet-powered Shaheds move at 400 km/h, he noted, and the Starshield speed limits were reduced to 70 km/h. Our Defense ministry is in touch and my partners, they told me that there were signals from the White House that they would return these capabilities. Have they returned the previous, previous, speed limits? No. But is it coming back now? Yes. UPDATE 1130 GMT: Hungary’s Prime Minister Péter Magyar has commented on his first meeting with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky. Magyar replaced the pro-Kremlin Viktor Orbán, who had led Hungary the previous 12 years, after victory in April’s Parliamentary elections. Magyar welcomed the Ukrainian Parliament’s adoption of a new law on minority education, including for ethnic Hungarians, as “a first step towards restoring mutual trust”. He said the two sides will “continue consultations … at the ministerial level”: “We agreed that it is in the interest of both countries to place their political and economic relations on a new foundation.” Magyar declared his solidarity with Zelensky “in the face of inhumane Russian aggression against his country”: “Hungary stands ready to provide assistance, through all available diplomatic means, towards achieving an immediate ceasefire and a lasting peace.” UPDATE 1124 GMT: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky has hailed his meeting, at the European Union summit, with European Council President António Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky cited the latest Russian attacks, including the murder of two civilians and injuring of 17 in Kharkiv city. Right now, there are no signals from Russia that it is ready to end its war. The signals it is sending point to something entirely different and certainly do not bring peace any closer…. European leadership is needed to ensure that people’s lives are sufficiently protected from this Russian terror. Zelensky cited discussions on air defense, energy, financial resilience, and Ukraine’s candidacy for EU membership. UPDATE 0853 GMT: At least three civilians have been murdered and seven injured in Ukraine’s second city Kharkiv by Russian strikes. Around 370,000 customers lost power in the Volyn region in western Ukraine as Russia damaged civilian and critical infrastructure facilities. Ukraine’s air defenses intercepted 114 of 149 drones fired by Russia overnight. Strikes were recorded at 24 locations. UPDATE 0846 GMT: Ukraine’s supply of Patriot interceptor missiles is critically low, say Kyiv’s officials. One said “only a couple” of Patriot missiles remain, after an October 7 supply of ten was depleted to counter Russian attacks on Kyiv. Another said there are no missiles at all. UPDATE 0829 GMT: Arriving with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen at a European Union leaders’ meeting in Brussels, European Council President António Costa said the EU’s support to Ukraine “remains as strong as ever”. In an implicit message to the Trump Administration, Costa made clear: This is no time to withdraw the support to Ukraine. This is no time to relieve Russia’s sanctions. This is essential to bring Russia to accept a real ceasefire, to bring Russia to the table of negotiations and to stop this war. He said to Zelensky, “You can count on us not only to support you in war, but most important for your future as a member of the European Union.” Von der Leyen called out Moscow’s attacks on energy infrastructure and said, “One thing is absolutely clear: we will not lift any sanctions unless Russia stops the war.” She said discussions will include support for Kyiv through the winter and defining Ukraine’s path to the European Union as two more “negotiating clusters” are opened, bringing the total to four of six required for accession. Zelensky responded that he is happy to have “huge support” from “leaders, real leaders”. Ukraine wants the war to end as soon as possible, but there are “no signals from the Russian side that they are ready to end this war. “That’s why we have to prepare for the winter” over defense and energy, he explained. ORIGINAL ENTRY: The White House issued the order to limit Ukraine’s access to Starshield, the military version of Starlink, earlier this week, according to “two US officials and a Western official briefed on the matter”. The restriction scuttled Ukrainian missions on the frontline and undermined Ukraine’s air defenses, putting civilians and US personnel at risk from Russia’s missile and drone strikes. The ⁠officials said leaders at the Defense ⁠Department received a message that the service for the Ukrainian military needed to be slowed. They did not identify who in the White House made the decision or who was responsible for implementing the order. A “senior US official” denied that the request came from Donald Trump. Ukrainian officials said service had been restored on Thursday. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and UK counterpart Wes Streeting, meeting in Washington, highlighted the restoration. They did not explain the cause of the outage although Streeting said, “This is not the first time we’ve seen a falling out between Washington and Kyiv.” Allies rallied behind Ukraine at a European Union summit in Brussels, attended by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday said it was “crucial” that Ukraine receive “all the means necessary to protect itself” after meeting Zelensky. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk posted, “I can reassure you, dear Ukrainian friends and President Zelensky: YOU ARE NOT ALONE.” On Thursday, after the latest Russian strikes, Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky also referred to the cutoff of early-warning intelligence and Donald Trump’s agreement to purchase Russian diesel fuel: It is important that our partners help us defend against this. Residential buildings, stores, energy and other critical infrastructure are under attack virtually nonstop. Not a single hour of peace. What is happening is Russia’s pointed response to the signals it is receiving from America. Unfortunately, there are dangerous signals about the possibility of further sanctions relief.
